draft.title: Physical influences on liveability
card: Physical influences are features of the natural environment. They affect how comfortable and safe a place is to live in.
Climate
the usual weather of a place over many years. Extreme heat, cold or rainfall can make daily life harder, while mild weather can make it easier.
Natural hazards
events such as floods, bushfires and cyclones that can harm people and property. Places that face them often have a lower liveability for safety.
Landforms, water and green space
Steep or rugged land can make building and travel harder. A reliable water supply and nearby parks, bushland or beaches can make a place more pleasant to live in.
draft.remember: Natural features such as weather, hazards, land, water and green space shape how comfortable and safe a place is.

a.q: Which of these is a physical influence on the liveability of a town?
opts: How often the town is hit by floods
How many cars use its main road
How expensive its houses are
How loud its night-time traffic is
a.why: Floods are a natural hazard, which is part of the natural environment. Traffic, housing costs and noise from cars come from human activity, so they are not physical influences.
a.clue: Look for the one that comes from nature, not from people.

b.q: Two towns in NSW have the same shops and schools. Town A has a river that sometimes floods homes. Town B has a reliable water supply and a large park. Why might Town B be seen as more liveable?
opts: It has fewer natural hazards and more green space
It has more services and facilities than Town A
It has a stronger sense of connection among families
It has lower crime and less traffic than Town A
b.why: Town B has a reliable water supply and a park, and it does not face flood danger. These are physical influences on comfort and safety. The question says the services are the same, so services cannot explain the difference.
b.clue: The shops and schools are the same, so look at the natural features.

a.best: How often the town is hit by floods

b.best: It has fewer natural hazards and more green space

problems.detail: The stem never says Town B is free of floods or other hazards. It only says Town B has a reliable water supply and a park. Both the right option ('fewer natural hazards') and the why ('it does not face flood danger') rely on an unstated inference. Adding something like 'Town B does not flood' to the stem would fix this.
